parts.name: Temporalis tendon
parts.function_note: The muscle's broad, fan-shaped origin from the entire temporal fossa converges as it descends deep to the zygomatic arch into a single strong tendon inserting on the coronoid process -- a fan-to-cord convergence pattern architecturally similar to (though not modeled with separate parts here, unlike) the quadriceps and rotator cuff tendons' documented internal layering.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The convergent tendon of one of the four muscles of mastication; its extensive fan-shaped origin funneling to a single narrow coronoid insertion is a clear architectural example of a fan-to-cord (convergent) muscle-tendon unit.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

proximal_attachment.landmark: posterior belly (2nd pharyngeal arch, facial n.)

distal_attachment.landmark: body/greater horn of the hyoid bone, via a fibrous sling (pulley loop) rather than a direct bony insertion

parts.name: Intermediate tendon and fibrous sling
parts.function_note: The rounded tendon joining digastric's two embryologically distinct bellies perforates the stylohyoid muscle and is held down to the hyoid bone by a fibrous loop (a sling derived from the pretracheal/deep cervical fascia) that allows the tendon to glide -- a genuine fibro-osseous pulley system, not a simple muscle-to-bone insertion, and directly analogous in mechanism to the finger flexor tendons' annular pulleys. This anchoring at the hyoid is what converts the two bellies' contraction into hyoid elevation/mandibular depression rather than the bellies simply sliding past one another.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.
parts.attachment_or_location: hyoid bone, body/greater horn, via the fibrous pulley loop

function: The fibro-osseous pulley connecting digastric's anterior and posterior bellies at the hyoid bone -- a standalone tendon structure by virtue of its pulley sling, distinct from either belly's own muscular anatomy.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

distal_attachment.landmark: posterior surface of the clavicle and first costal cartilage, via a fascial sling that binds the tendon to the clavicle rather than a direct bony insertion

parts.name: Intermediate tendon and fascial sling
parts.function_note: The short tendon joining omohyoid's inferior and superior bellies is bound down close to the clavicle by a fascial sling continuous with the sheath of the great vessels/pretracheal fascia, changing the muscle's line of pull the way the digastric sling does at the hyoid. Clinically relevant as a fixed deep-neck landmark for the internal jugular vein and as a cause of a visible neck band in some 'omohyoid syndrome' cases.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.
parts.attachment_or_location: posterior clavicle/1st costal cartilage region, via the fascial pulley sling

function: The fibro-osseous pulley connecting omohyoid's inferior and superior bellies near the clavicle -- a standalone tendon structure by virtue of its fascial sling, which redirects the muscle's line of pull much as the digastric sling does at the hyoid.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
